Stilleverwahrer des Vorhofs: Keeper of Silence of the Forecourt
Ein Halbgott steht wieder in der Schlang: A demigod stands in the queue before the Courts again, as old as a city. He recognises your scar. "You were here once before. Back then you were ash. Let's see what you are now."
Der Halbgott fällt auf die Knie. Unter i: The demigod falls to his knees. Beneath him the white stone gives way, and he slides down, through the clouds, to Calderwick. Up here no one dies. They just become too light.
Diesmal verbrennst du nicht. Du wirst nu:
This time you do not burn. You only become too light. The white stone lets go of you, and you fall, through the clouds you already know, until Calderwick catches you again.

Vera enters you into the Book of the Fallen a second time. Under "Cause" she writes this time: too early.
Du ziehst dich zum Bahnsteig zurück. Hie: You withdraw to the platform. Up here no one follows you. They have time.
Ein Heiliger unterbricht sein Gebet und: A saint interrupts his prayer and looks at your scar. "A saint with a scar. That is rare. Most of you stay down below."
Der Heilige beendet sein Gebet nicht. Er: The saint does not finish his prayer. He collapses into himself, and the light he prayed with trickles down through the joints of the stone.
Er betet. Die Welt unter den Wolken antw: He prays. The world beneath the clouds answers: +8 defence.
Diesmal sieht der Engel dich an. Er hat: This time the angel looks at you. It has no eyes, only light that falls where eyes would be, and it falls on your scar. It raises its wings.
Der Engel fällt nicht. Er legt die Flüge: The angel does not fall. It folds its wings and steps aside, as if you had answered a question correctly. Behind it the ridge is clear.
Der Engel schweigt. Das Schweigen legt s: The angel is silent. The silence settles around it like armour: +12 defence.
Der Engel öffnet den Mund. Kein Laut kom: The angel opens its mouth. No sound comes out, but the clouds beneath the ridge tear open.
Starling sitzt auf der untersten Stufe d:
Starling sits on the lowest step of the throne, freezing. He wears two coats, one over the other. "You turned off the pipe," he says. "Of course. My best investigator."

He stands up, slowly, like an old man. Then not slowly any more. "Up here you weigh as much as you have harvested. I have harvested a great deal."
Starling fällt auf die Stufen. Der Stein:
Starling falls onto the steps. The stone beneath him turns soft, and he sinks into it, as into water. "Forty-one years," he says, and it sounds almost relieved. "I had forgotten what it is like to fall."

Then he is gone. Somewhere beneath the clouds, early tomorrow morning, Vera Darnell will write a name into the Book of the Fallen that she has written once before.
Starling watches you fall. "Resubmission," he says, the way Wetherby would have said it.

This time you do not burn. You only become too light. The white stone lets go of you, and you fall, through the clouds you already know, until Calderwick catches you again.

Vera enters you into the Book of the Fallen a second time. Under "Cause" she writes this time: too early.
Starling zieht den Mantel enger. Das Lic: Starling pulls his coat tighter. The light around him turns cold and hard: +12 defence.
Starling steht auf. Ohne die Leitung aus: Starling stands up. Without the pipe from Briarholt he has grown lighter, and he knows it. He reaches for the throne behind him, and the throne lets him.
Der Schaffner ohne Gesicht nimmt den Bür: The faceless conductor takes the letter of guarantee, reads every signature and hands it back. "You have guarantors. Now show me what you weigh. Demigods burn up on the journey. Saints only once they are up there."
Der Schaffner locht den Bürgschein, einm: The conductor punches the letter of guarantee, once for every signature. "Whoever is still standing travels. Whoever lies on the floor has good guarantors and too little weight."
Der Schaffner legt dir den Bürgschein au: The conductor lays the letter of guarantee on your chest, neatly folded. "Good guarantors," he says. "Too little weight. Come back as a saint."
Du trittst vom Gleis zurück. Der Schaffn: You step back from the track. The conductor waits. He has been waiting for years.
Der Schaffner reißt die Uniform auf. Dar: The conductor tears open his uniform. Beneath it there is no light like the first time, but a track that leads upwards.
Die Himmelsstadt, zum zweiten Mal: The Sky City, a Second Time
Derselbe weiße Bahnsteig, dieselben Wolk:
The same white platform, the same clouds. But this time the place does not weigh you. You stand.

Your scar pulls, as if it remembered. The beings up here feel it too: they look at you now instead of through you. Whatever looks at you can fall. And so can you.
Der Schaffner ohne Gesicht hält die Tür: The faceless conductor holds the door open. "Down to Calderwick? The ticket is valid both ways. You paid for it."
Auf dem Thron sitzt niemand, und doch is:
No one sits on the throne, and yet it is full. This time you do not burn. The Old One looks at you, for a long time, the way one looks at a piece of work that is not yet finished.

Then he speaks, without a mouth, without a sound. It is only a weight that settles on you, and you understand it all the same: he has lost a hand. He does not need a new one. He needs someone who sits across from him.

Above the angel, above the first sequence, there is no throne for servants. Sequence 0.

The ground lets go of you, gently this time. You do not fall. You are sent down.
Über dem Kronenarchiv endet ein Gleis in:
Above the Crown Archive a track ends in mid-air. A conductor without a face waits beside it, for years now, people say.

"The train upwards is running again," he says. "Not for everyone. Whoever wants to last up there comes as a saint, and even saints burn there without guarantors."

He holds out an empty letter of guarantee. "Five of the fallen must sign for you. People who live down here and know what happens up there. Then I will test your weight."
Der Schaffner ohne Gesicht nimmt den Bür:
The faceless conductor takes the letter of guarantee. Five names, five hands. He nods and steps in front of the carriage door.

"The guarantors are good. Now your weight."
Du steigst ein. Diesmal kippt der Boden:
You get in. This time the floor does not tip away, it rises. The train travels through smoke, through clouds, through the light that burned you the first time. It still burns. But you remain.

Your scar glows the whole journey long.
Du drehst das Ventil zu. Das Rohr wird k:
You close the valve. The pipe goes cold, from the bottom up, so slowly that you can watch it. Somewhere above Calderwick, above the clouds, a man now sits on the steps of a throne and freezes.

He will not come down any more. If you want him, you have to go up. As a saint you would still burn there. As an angel perhaps not.

Above the Crown Archive in Calderwick a faceless conductor waits for people the fallen will vouch for.
Aufzugswärter am Gleisfuß. Fiel vor zwan: Lift keeper at the Track's Foot. Fell twenty years ago as a demigod of the Clock.
Silas hält die Bremskurbel mit beiden Hä: Silas holds the brake crank with both hands. "I used to be faster than this lift. Now I wait for it, like everyone else."
Was weißt du von oben?: What do you know about up there?
„Ich kurble die Gefallenen von der Aufsc: "I crank the fallen up from the impact site into the city. Whoever rides for the first time looks up. Whoever rides for the second time looks at his shoes."
„Oben vergeht die Zeit nicht. Sie wird v: "Up there time does not pass. It is administered. I once asked who it belongs to. After that I was here."
Silas zieht die Bremse an, bis der Aufzu: Silas pulls the brake until the lift creaks and signs on the crank housing. "You made the railway honest. Up there that counts for nothing. Down here it does."
„Bürgen? Für jemanden, der mir noch nich: "Vouch? For someone who hasn't even helped me with the railway? See to the seventh stop, then we'll talk."
Rohrpostbote. Kind zweier Gefallener, in: Pneumatic post messenger. Child of two fallen, born in Calderwick.
„Ich bin der Einzige hier, der nie oben: "I'm the only one here who has never been up there. My parents both fell. I'm what came of it."
„Ich bringe Kapseln. Die meisten sind le: "I deliver capsules. Most are empty, because people forget what they wanted to write. The burning takes your sentences with it."
„Meine Mutter sagt, oben riecht es nach: "My mother says up there smells of nothing. My father says of bread. I think they were up there on different days."
Oskar unterschreibt in großen, ungeübten: Oskar signs in big, unpractised letters. "Ida said you opened the lid with your bare hands. That's enough for me."
„Ida hat mir immer den Rest ihres Brots: "Ida always gave me the rest of her bread. Since she's been gone, nobody gives me anything. Bring her back, then I'll sign anything."
Laternenwart. Fiel als Halbgott der Late: Lamplighter. Fell as a demigod of the Lantern and since then lights only street lamps.
„Früher habe ich Dinge gesehen, die noch: "I used to see things that had not happened yet. Now I see whether the wick is dry. It is more restful."
„In Calderwick brennt keine Laterne von: "In Calderwick no lamp burns by itself. The monsters like the dark, so do the fallen. I'm the only one who doesn't."
„Oben brauchst du kein Licht. Alles leuc: "Up there you need no light. Everything shines. That is why you see nothing there that you are not meant to see."
Enno hält den Bürgschein gegen seine Lat: Enno holds the letter of guarantee against his lantern until the ink dries. "A guild head. Good. Up there, there are only heads."
„Ich bürge für Leute, die schon einmal e: "I vouch for people who have already faced a guild head in their own quarter. Whoever can't do that burns up there in the first hour."
Griffmacherin. Macht Griffe für Hände, d: Handle maker. Makes handles for hands that were burned up there.
„Zeig mir deine Hände. Nein, die Innense: "Show me your hands. No, the palms. Hm. Not burned enough yet to be my customer."
„Wer oben verbrannt wird, kann danach of: "Whoever is burned up there often can't hold anything hot afterwards. I make handles from horn and cork. For pots, for swords, for door handles."
„Ich war nie oben. Ich mache nur die Gri: "I was never up there. I only make the handles for those who were. You learn a lot about a place when you see what it does to hands."
Hanna nimmt das Geld, zählt es nicht und: Hanna takes the money, doesn't count it, and signs with a pair of pliers dipped in ink. "No handle lasts forever. A signature does."
„Eine Bürgschaft ist ein Werkstück wie j: "A guarantee is a piece of work like any other. Two thousand five hundred shillings, and I'll put my name under it."
Nachtsetzer. Setzt das Fallbuch jede Nac: Night typesetter. Sets the Book of the Fallen in lead every night so that it does not burn.
„Psst. Ich setze gerade einen Namen. Wen: "Shh. I'm setting a name. If I misread it, tomorrow the wrong person is in the book."
"Vera writes in ink. Ink burns. Every night I set each entry again in lead. Lead burns too, but slower."
„Ich setze seit zwölf Jahren Namen von G: "I've been setting the names of the fallen for twelve years. I know up there only from letters. They are always the same: burned."
Arvo setzt deinen Namen in Blei, drückt: Arvo sets your name in lead, presses it onto the letter of guarantee and blows on it. "Ruth traced the stroke back. Whoever makes that possible gets my name."
„Zwölf Einträge sind gestrichen, und kei: "Twelve entries are struck out, and nobody can tell me who struck them. As long as that's so, I sign nothing that goes into a book."
Marktfrau am Quittungsmarkt. Zahlt in di: Market woman at the Receipt Market. Pays into the Fund of the Fallen.
„Kartoffeln, Salz, Kerzen. Keine Federn,: "Potatoes, salt, candles. No feathers, no halos. Whoever wants to sell that kind of thing goes to Lottie."
„Ich verkaufe, was Gefallene essen. Sie: "I sell what the fallen eat. They eat a lot. Whoever is burned has to become heavy again."
„Ich will nicht hinauf. Ich will, dass h: "I don't want to go up. I want nobody down here to harvest any more. Every week I pay into Pritch's fund so that it stops."
Selma wischt sich die Hände an der Schür: Selma wipes her hands on her apron and signs. "Two fewer who harvest. I'll vouch for that."
„Ich zahle in die Kasse, und du kassiers: "I pay into the fund, and you collect from it. Settle two of Pritch's notices, then I'll know my money is worth something."
Fensterputzerin am Kronenarchiv. Sieht v: Window cleaner at the Crown Archive. Sees from outside what happens inside.
„Ich putze die Fenster des Kronenarchivs: "I clean the windows of the Crown Archive. From outside. None of us may look in, but glass is glass."
„Ich habe jahrelang gesehen, wie Kisten: "For years I watched crates being carried out of the archive. I kept cleaning. I am ashamed of it."
„Ich fiel als Halbengel des Fadens. Oben: "I fell as a half-angel of the Thread. Up there I thought I was someone who looks. Down here I learned that looking is not enough."
Mira unterschreibt mit dem Finger, nass: Mira signs with her finger, wet from the wash water, and then in ink over it. "You did what I didn't dare to."
„Solange Wetherby hinter meinen Fenstern: "As long as Wetherby sits behind my windows, I sign nothing that goes up. He has his hand on the second train."
Wäscherin. Wäscht die verbrannten Kleide: Washerwoman. Washes the burned clothes of the fallen.
Dora sieht dir nicht ins Gesicht, sonder: Dora doesn't look at your face but at your chest. "There it is. The scar. Everyone who falls has one. Yours is still glowing."
„Ich wasche, was von oben kommt. Ruß geh: "I wash what comes from up there. Soot comes out, blood comes out. Light never. The clothes still glow for years when you put the light out."
„Die Narbe ist das Einzige, was man von: "The scar is the only thing you bring back from up there. It doesn't hurt. But when you go up again, they recognise you by it. And you them."
Dora legt ihre Hand flach auf deine Narb: Dora lays her hand flat on your scar, only briefly, and then signs. "Whoever has burned once knows what to be afraid of. That is a good start."
„Du hast keine Narbe. Dann warst du nie: "You have no scar. Then you were never up there, and then I can't vouch for you."
Archivdienerin. Staubt nachts die Regist: Archive servant. Dusts the registers in the Crown Archive at night.
„Nachts ist das Archiv ehrlich. Keiner s: "At night the archive is honest. Nobody sorts, nobody strikes out. Only me and the dust."
"I dust the registers. Nothing more. But whoever wipes dust reads along. I know which files never gather dust, because they are opened every day."
„Meine Mutter fiel, als ich klein war. S: "My mother fell when I was small. She can no longer count the stairs, but she still knows what the throne sounds like. Like a breath that never ends."
Berta pustet den Staub vom Bürgschein un: Berta blows the dust off the letter of guarantee and signs in an archivist's hand. "Neat. They like that up there."
„Ich unterschreibe nur, was gebunden ist: "I only sign what is bound. Loose pages fly away. Have Klammer bind you a file, then I'll know you are careful."
Vera schlägt das Fallbuch auf, ganz hint:
Vera opens the Book of the Fallen at the very back. The last entry is fresh.

"Lucius Starling. Fell early today. Pathway: illegible. Sequence 2. Cause: burned." Beneath it she has drawn a line with a ruler, not upwards but across.

"He lies in Bexley's Widows' Terrace and speaks to no one," she says. "For the first time in forty-one years he is down here as just one of us."
Starling sitzt oben vor dem Thron und fr: Starling sits up there before the throne and freezes, ever since the pipe from Briarholt went cold. He no longer comes down. Above the Crown Archive the second train runs, but only for saints the fallen vouch for. This time, whoever loses up there falls. You too.
Finde den zweiten Zug über dem Kronenarc: Find the second train above the Crown Archive
Sammle 5 Bürgschaften von Gefallenen in: Collect 5 guarantees from the fallen in Calderwick
Besiege den Schaffner ohne Gesicht: Defeat the Conductor Without a Face
Tritt vor den Thron des Alten: Step before the throne of the Old One
Five signatures for the second train. Five people who say: that one is heavy enough. Most here don't get a single one.
Die Narbe? Jeder hat eine. Oben erkennen: The scar? Everyone has one. Up there they recognise you by it. Whether that's good, nobody knows.
Starling ist gefallen, sagen sie. Er lie: Starling has fallen, they say. He lies at Bexley's and speaks to no one. Nobody here harvests for him any more.
Oben wurdest du verbrannt. Die Narbe ble: Up there you were burned. The scar remains. The beings of the Sky City recognise it: you hit them {0} % harder, they hit you {1} % harder.
